findings.finding: The plan describes a destructive/irreversible operation (`--repair` writes durable LINK/UNLINK events) and names a `pre-doctor-repair` tag as a "rollback anchor", but never specifies the back-out procedure an operator would follow to actually undo a repair run. Identifying a reference point is not the same as a rollback plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (in the plan or the help text) the recovery path when a partial repair creates an ambiguous-pair: either instruct operators to roll back to the pre-doctor-repair tag OID, or add a `--force-unlink` escape hatch, or have the repair driver detect 'self-created ambiguity' (replacement OID matches the current run) and complete the unlink automatically.
evidence: '--repair writes the replacement link BEFORE removing the stale one, so an interruption leaves a superset the next run converges'
'It declines a pair whose pair-scoped UNLINK would cancel a different relation (ambiguous-pair)'
No documented recovery path when the superset itself becomes the ambiguous-pair case after a partial repair
findings.finding: If the pre-doctor-repair tag write succeeds but a subsequent replacement-write also succeeds while its paired unlink-write fails, the next run will observe two net-active links on that ordered pair and classify it as ambiguous-pair — which the plan explicitly declines to repair. The plan does not document how an operator recovers from this stuck state (neither auto-repair nor a documented manual path), making a partial repair self-locking until the operator intervenes with raw event writes.
findings.location: Approach section (repair ordering paragraph) and AC: 'An ordered pair carrying two net-active links is reported unrepairable with reason ambiguous-pair'
scenarios: Repair run is interrupted between the replacement-write and the unlink-write (e.g. SIGKILL, disk full, lock timeout). On resume, the pair has two net-active links. The scanner classifies it ambiguous-pair and refuses to repair it. The operator has no documented path to resolution short of manual event surgery.
findings.suggested_fix: In the repair driver, after writing the replacement link, record its event OID. On a subsequent run, when classifying ambiguous-pair, check whether one of the two links was written by a prior doctor repair run (detectable via event metadata or a doctor-written marker). If so, treat it as a resumable partial repair and proceed with the unlink rather than declining. Document this behaviour in the plan and help text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what `--repair` does when the `pre-doctor-repair` tag write fails: abort with a clear error and non-zero exit before writing any repair events, and add a test case that injects a tag-write failure and asserts no repair events were written.
evidence: Plan text: 'force-writes a pre-doctor-repair tag at the pre-run OID as a rollback anchor'
No AC or Approach text specifies the failure mode for the tag write itself: abort repair, warn and continue, or other.
The tag write is the only rollback safety net; its failure path is the highest-consequence unspecified error in the repair flow.
findings.finding: The plan requires that the `pre-doctor-repair` tag is force-written before the first repair event write, but specifies no behavior if that tag write itself fails (permissions error, disk-full, store corruption). A silent failure here removes the rollback anchor before any repair events are written, so the user proceeds with an unprotected repair and has no documented way to know the anchor was not placed.
findings.location: Approach: 'It force-writes a `pre-doctor-repair` tag at the pre-run OID as a rollback anchor'; AC bullet 10.
scenarios: On a read-only-mounted filesystem or a store with a permissions misconfiguration, the tag write silently fails; `--repair` either proceeds without a rollback anchor (silent data hazard) or crashes with an unhandled exception, in both cases leaving the operator unable to recover a partially-repaired store.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach and a matching AC: 'If the pre-doctor-repair tag write fails, --repair exits immediately with a non-zero code and writes no events; verified by injecting a tag-write error and asserting the event-file count is unchanged.'
